item: The extraction lock has a live gauge: seconds held and thread-seconds waited are kept as cumulative totals, so an open hold, an open wait and a pass that never ends are all readable
status: shipped (local bundle, draft PR to follow)
summary: lock_stats recorded a hold only when it ENDED and the pass monitor resets the window every pass, so a crashed pass, a hang or an 85 s hold left nothing to read. lock_stats now also keeps two cumulative totals for the life of the process (seconds the lock was held, thread-seconds spent waiting for it) behind a private leaf lock that reset() does not touch, and live_reading() adds the part of a hold and of each wait still open at the instant of the reading, with holder_age_s and the number waiting. Both totals only grow, so the difference of two readings is exact for the interval between them. extract_article marks asking (before the lock, inside the outer try), holding (first line inside the hold), released (finally, after the hold's end stamp) and, through record(), gave_up when the lock was never taken; the clock is read under the gauge's lock so a held fraction can never exceed the elapsed time. Nothing reads the gauge yet (the monitor block waits for the governor PR). Proof: 15 tests, among them an eight-thread run checked against an independent log built from the gauge's own clock reads (tolerance 1e-6) and 18 mutants all killed. Cost, measured alone on the machine: the three marks take 1.5 microseconds per extraction (about 1 microsecond inside the hold) against a 4 ms extraction of an 8 KB page on one thread; in the real collector at 14 collectors, lock on, pins trafilatura 2.1.0 / lxml 6.1.1, three alternating runs per tree, base against gauge: 8 KB pages 472 articles/min on base (440 to 476) against 463 (455 to 473) with the gauge, mean hold 35.2 against 35.4 ms, lock held share 26.8 against 27.3 percent; 64 KB pages 134 (127 to 141) against 136 (134 to 138) articles/min, mean hold 284 against 286 ms, held share 63.7 against 64.0 percent: no difference beyond the spread of three runs. Not shown: the longest single hold and the longest single wait read higher in two of three gauge runs at 8 KB (median 0.75 against 0.56 s and 0.95 against 0.77 s; one event per run, not seen at 64 KB, which uses the same marks, and the mean hold did not move), so a small effect on a single event is not excluded. Cross-check on the same six gauge runs: the gauge's growth over the measured passes equals the pass window's hold total and wait total to within 1.5 ms over totals of 22 to 615 s, with nobody waiting and no holder at the end. Known edges, stated in the code: an unmatched release is clamped, and a KeyboardInterrupt landing exactly inside released() could leave a phantom holder in the gauge (best effort, never an extraction's result). Not measured: a store with real article history, other core counts, real network time.
